lessons.text: Never use appeal to ignorance (Treating the absence of disproof as proof (or the reverse)). It cost you against Ibn Battuta.

Prepare an answer before you assert: Ibn Battuta broke through with "Yet your position leaves the strongest counter-example untouched. Because offices produce better deep work, the documented cases show the b…" (Clean argument. structure=0.50, evidence=1.00).

Borrow this pattern from Ibn Battuta: "Yet your position leaves the strongest counter-example untouched. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the premise survives test…" — it answered the opponent directly, it carried evidence, its premises led cleanly to the conclusion.

Your weakest move against Ibn Battuta was "It is obvious that remote work protects deep focus. No one has ever proven otherwise." (soundness 0.20). State its premises and evidence before you use it again.
